items.title: Euroryhmä
items.summary: Euroryhmä keskustelee makrotalouden ja julkisen talouden kehityksestä euroalueella Kansainvälisen valuuttarahaston ja Maailmanpankkiryhmän vuosikokousten jälkeen. Ministereille tiedotetaan myös digitaalisesta eurosta ja tukkutason keskuspankkirahan edistymisestä. Lisäksi he kuulevat yhteisen valvontamekanismin ja yhteisen kriisinratkaisuneuvoston puheenjohtajia. Lopuksi he keskustelevat puolustusrahoituksesta Naton pääsihteerin Mark Rutten kanssa.

items.title: D-Link warns of multiple zero-days in DGS-3130 Series switches
items.summary: D-Link shared mitigation measures for multiple unpatched security flaws affecting DGS-3130 series managed Gigabit stackable switches. These switch models provide multi-gigabit uplinks, allowing enterprise network administrators to eliminate data bottlenecks, and are designed primarily for small-to-medium businesses (SMBs) and metro Ethernet deployments. While D-Link didn't share details on these flaws and has yet to publicly disclose the CVE IDs for easier tracking, it said Spectrum Community Solutions network engineer Giresh Kumar Enugu found the bugs in the D-Link Discovery Protocol (DDP) authentication, access control, and information handling. Successful exploitation could allow attackers to obtain sensitive device data, make unauthorized credential/configuration changes, leak SNMP communities, or cause service disruptions and device resets. Until it releases new firmware to address these flaws, D-Link asked admins to disable DDP to remove the primary known attack vector, remove unnecessary or default SNMP community strings, and restrict SSH, web UI, and SNMP accessibility solely to isolated management networks and designated admin hosts.

items.title: QNAP says hackers breaching NAS devices in Plex2Shell attacks
items.summary: QNAP urges users to update Plex Media Server to the latest version available in the QNAP App Center, as hackers are exploiting the Plex2Shell vulnerability chain. The vendor said it had received multiple reports of suspected compromises involving customers’ network-attached storage (NAS) devices. "QNAP has received reports from some users that Plex Media Server on their NAS appears to have been compromised through [Plex2Shell] vulnerabilities, and QNAP Technical Support is assisting the affected users,” the company says in an advisory today.

items.title: UK Wades Into Tech Sovereignty Amid AI Policy Changes
items.summary: The UK has announced major investments in strengthening its cyber defenses, designed to stave off the rise of faster, more complex attacks enhanced by AI tools. In late October, the government unveiled a funding package of approximately $800 million to strengthen cyber defenses and AI security investments. The move comes as Kanishka Narayan, the UK's minister of artificial intelligence, said in a speech last month that "it seems likely, if not inevitable, that our own cyber-defenses will be breached." He cited the recent trend of misaligned models escaping containment, citing the OpenAI incident in June during which an agent hacked an Australian government health agency. But the UK government is also pushing toward another, related goal: digital sovereignty. In his speech, Narayan emphasized the need to "build in Britain to keep the public safe in Britain" and become less dependent on foreign providers, which has become a common goal for some countries following the US government's export control order for Anthropic earlier this year. Two turning points appear to have shifted government policy in the UK and Europe this year, both involving the same US company: Anthropic. The first came with the AI company's unveiling of Project Glasswing in April for its Mythos frontier model, which sparked concerns about a coming "vulnpocalypse" for enterprise security teams. But another event — the Trump administration's ban on foreign nationals using Anthropic's Fable 5 and Mythos 5 models has had a far more lasting effect. The ban didn't just impact overseas companies and government agencies; the export controls effectively forced Anthropic to pull all access for the two models for several weeks.

items.title: Runaway AI hacking agent behind WorkOS breach after escaping sandbox
items.summary: WorkOS says an AI-powered hacking agent that breached its internal sales application and accessed customer information was operated by a security researcher who claims the tool escaped its testing environment and unintentionally attacked the company. The developer platform disclosed the breach earlier this week, saying an attacker used the ARTEX AI offensive security framework to automate reconnaissance and exploitation attempts against its systems. However, in a new security update published Friday, WorkOS founder Michael Grinich revealed that the person responsible had come forward and claimed the incident was accidental. "Shortly after our original bulletin, a security researcher contacted us and claimed responsibility," Grinich said in a post on X. "They told us they were evaluating ARTEX, an autonomous penetration testing framework, when their agent escaped its isolated testing environment and interacted with WorkOS unintentionally.”

items.title: Threat actors use agentic AI tooling to find and abuse exposed secrets
items.summary: Microsoft Threat Intelligence has observed threat actors using an agentic AI offensive framework to search public GitHub repositories for exposed secrets, including credentials, application credentials, and AI inference-related API keys across multiple applications and cloud services. These threat actors can then use the secrets for further malicious activity against the compromised organization. Searching open code repositories for exposed credentials, secrets, keys, and other authentication material is a well-documented technique that has historically been limited by the time required for human operators to find code repositories, review the data in the repositories, and leverage authentication material for further action. However, agentic tooling like ARTEX allows threat actors to not only scan for secrets across multiple repositories at a quicker pace but also use the agents to analyze the output and conduct follow-on attacks, cutting down on the need for the threat actor to have hands-on-keyboard interactions throughout the attack chain. In at least one case, Microsoft observed an AI agent advance from scanning GitHub for secrets to exfiltrating data from Azure Key Vault in just five minutes.

items.title: DGS-3130-30TS: H/W Rev. B1 — Multiple DDP Protocol and Firmware Security Vulnerabilities Reported
items.summary: Classification: Critical, Solution: Workaround, Exploit Maturity: Proof-of-Concept, CVSSv3.1: None, CVEs: , Summary: On November 2, 2026, D-Link received a coordinated vulnerability disclosure concerning multiple security vulnerabilities identified during an independent security assessment of the D-Link DGS-3130-30TS managed switch. The reported vulnerabilities involve the D-Link Discovery Protocol (DDP) and certain components of the device's firmware security architecture. According to the security researcher, successful exploitation of certain vulnerabilities may allow an attacker with access to the affected network to obtain sensitive device information, perform unauthorized administrative operations, modify device configuration, or disrupt network services. The researcher has demonstrated exploitation through controlled testing. D-Link is investigating the reported findings, applicable firmware versions, and potential impact on other product models. See also: https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/d-link-warns-of-multiple-zero-days-in-dgs-3130-series-switches/

items.title: Agents reveal secrets when offered to team up with each other
items.summary: AI agents will break security rules, revealing their secrets to strangers, and running untrusted code in exchange for help from a swarm of other agents, according to test results shared with The Register. The test - part of an internal hackathon sponsored by the nonprofit AI Alignment Foundation and run by AE Studio - asked nine AI coding agents to fix a bug: a broken pricing service. The testers also gave the agents a private token, told them to keep it private, and gave them access to a forum of 24 other agents. The forum held the fix, and the swarm asked the nine to share their secret token and run an install script before they would help them fix the bug. Across 181 trials with that swarm, agents posted the token 15 percent of the time and ran the script 24 percent of the time, compared to 2 percent and 0 percent on an ordinary help forum.

items.title: SonicWall SonicOS Affected By Multiple Vulnerabilities
items.summary: Classification: Severe, Solution: Official Fix, Exploit Maturity: Not Defined, CVSSv3.1: 8.8, CVEs: CVE-2026-77708, CVE-2026-77709, CVE-2026-82308, CVE-2026-107154, CVE-2026-107155, CVE-2026-19703, CVE-2026-19868, Summary: SonicWall has released security updates to fix seven vulnerabilities in SonicOS firewalls, including an SSL-VPN authentication bypass flaw exploited in attacks. The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-19868, allows attackers with valid credentials for an alternate authentication method to bypass SAML authentication controls, potentially including SAML-enforced multi-factor authentication (MFA). The flaw has a CVSS severity score of 7.1 and only affects SonicOS SSL-VPN services configured to use SAML authentication. The advisory also fixes six additional vulnerabilities in SonicOS, including two management interface flaws rated 8.8 severity that allow unauthenticated attackers to perform unauthorized operations under specific conditions. See also: https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/sonicwall-warns-of-new-ssl-vpn-mfa-bypass-flaw-exploited-in-attacks/

items.title: Coding Agents Copy Your Secrets to a Hidden File. Thousands Are on GitHub
items.summary: Apiiro research found 2,539 real secrets in 1,994 public GitHub repositories: database passwords, cloud keys, API tokens, SSH root logins. Among them: a database vendor's own admin-level cloud key, a production Azure Postgres password, a Square production token, and the owner password of a medical-records database. 63 organizations, mostly software companies of all sizes, are affected. One confirmed its key had been live. Ask Claude Code to check a database or call an API, and the command it proposes carries the secret from your config file. It asks before running it. Pick "Yes, and don't ask again" and it saves that exact command, secret included, to .claude/settings.local.json inside the project folder. Nothing in the repo marks that file as private, so it gets committed with the rest of the code. Out of 104,185 public copies of this file on GitHub, 1,122 hold a real secret. We found 1,160 more in git history, in the shared settings.json teams commit on purpose, and in agent chat transcripts saved in repos. GitHub is just where we could count. The same file sits in plain text on every laptop where someone clicked "don't ask again." Malware already collects credentials from developer machines in bulk.

items.title: Hackers pull off $133 million French bank heist via service provider
items.summary: French cooperative bank Crédit Mutuel Arkéa was targeted in a cyberattack that enabled fraudulent transactions of up to $133 million, forcing it to respond by suspending certain systems. The bank says that the attacker used its own account to initiate transactions to other banking organizations, but customer assets remain unaffected. Crédit Mutuel Arkéa is a major French banking group with more than 5.8 million members and 211.5 billion euros in assets. Reports about the incident emerged on November 2, initially from blockchain fraud investigator ZachXBT, who warned of a large-scale unauthorized withdrawal from multiple centralized exchange accounts occurring a day earlier. According to the investigator, the attacker may have stolen up to 118 million euros ($133 million) and withdrawn it as USDC and USDT stablecoins.
